paragraphs.source_en: The next step was the battle plan. Where was I to open hostilities with the mice? Naturally, wherever the mice appeared. No matter how advantageous a position I occupied, if I, one lone cat, merely took up my stance and sat waiting blankly for them to appear, it could not be called war. Thus arose the necessity of studying where the mice might come and go. Standing in the middle of the kitchen, I looked all around, trying to guess from which direction they would emerge. At that moment I felt as if I had truly become Admiral Togo. Osan, the maid, had gone to the bath and had not yet returned. The children had long since gone to sleep. After coming back from Imozaka, where he had eaten rice dumplings, the master had shut himself up as usual in his study. As for what the master's wife was doing, I had no idea. Most likely she was dozing and dreaming grand dreams of her yams. From time to time a rickshaw passed before the gate, and after it had gone by the surroundings seemed still more silent. My resolve, my high spirit, the aspect of the kitchen, and the silence all around: the entire atmosphere, one might say, was charged with tragic grandeur. In any case, I felt I might fairly be called the Admiral Togo of cats. Anyone who enters such a state will feel a certain pleasure amid the grimness, but I discovered that beneath this pleasure there in fact lay a very great anxiety. I had made up my mind to wage war on the mice, and I feared no number of them; yet not knowing from where they would appear was inconvenient in many ways. Combining the materials gathered from careful observation, I found that the mouse brigands had three possible routes of appearance. If they were sewer rats, they would surely follow the earthen pipe from the sink around to the back of the stove; in that case I would have to hide behind the fire-extinguishing jar and cut off their retreat. They might also crawl out through the plaster hole where bathwater drains into the ditch, circle around the bathroom, and suddenly appear in the kitchen; if so, I would take my position on the pot lid, and when they passed beneath my eyes I would leap down from above and seize one in a single grab. Then, looking around again, I noticed that the lower right corner of the cupboard door had been gnawed into a half-moon-shaped hole, quite possibly a convenient entrance and exit for mice. I sniffed at it with my nose, and sure enough there was a slight smell of mouse. If they came charging out from here, I would hide behind the pillar, let them pass, and strike them unexpectedly from the side with one swipe of my claws. If they came from the ceiling, I thought, and looked up: that ceiling, blackened by soot and lit by the dim kerosene lamp, looked as though hell had been turned upside down and hung there; with my abilities alone, I could never get up to it. I decided that the mice would surely not descend from such a height, and so I lifted my guard in that direction. Even so, I still worried that there was a danger of being attacked from three sides. If only one party came, I could deal with it with my eyes shut; if two came, I was confident I could somehow manage; but if three came, then however much I might be called an instinctive expert at catching mice, I would have no way to begin.

paragraphs.source_zh: 下一步就是作战计划啦。在什么地方与老鼠开战呢？当然是在老鼠出现的地方。不管我占有多么有利的地形，如果只是由我一个猫儿摆好架势呆呆等待它们的出现，是不能称为战争的。于是便出现了研究老鼠从哪里出没的必要。我站在厨房当中四面环视，捉摸他们会从哪里出现。这时我觉得仿佛自己真成了东乡大将啦。厨娘阿三去洗澡还没有回来。小孩们早已睡下。主人在芋坂吃罢糯米团子回来后一直缩在书斋里。至于主人的妻子在干什么我一无所知。大概她是在打瞌睡，在大做其山药的梦吧。不时有人力车从门前通过，车过去后周围更加显得岑寂。不论是我的决心还是我的壮志，也不论是厨房的光景和四周的岑寂，可以说整个气氛是充满了悲壮之感。不管怎么说，我觉得我可以算得上是猫中的东乡大将啦。任何人一旦进入这种境界，都会在凄惨之中感到某种愉快，但我发现在这种愉快的背后，实际是隐伏着一种极大的担忧。和老鼠打仗的决心我是下定了，不管来上几只老鼠我都无所畏惧，不过弄不清老鼠们会从哪里出现，却有许多不便之处。综合周密观察得来的材料，鼠贼有三条出没的路径。如果它们是下水道里的老鼠，那肯定会沿着瓦管从洗菜池那边绕到炉灶的后边去，若是那样，我就得藏在消火罐背后来切断它们的退路。也许它们会从地沟里排泄洗澡水的那个石灰孔里钻出来，绕过洗澡间突然出现在厨房里，若是这样，我就得据守在锅盖上，当它们从我眼下通过时，我会从上边一跃而下，一把抓住它。然后我又环顾了一下四周，壁橱门的右下角有个被咬破的半月形的洞，这很可能是老鼠出入方便的地方。我用鼻子嗅了嗅，果然有点老鼠味。如果它们从这里呐喊而来，我就要躲在柱子背后放它们走过去，从侧面出其不意地给它们一爪子。如果它们从顶棚上来呢，我仰头看了一下，那煤烟熏得漆黑的顶棚，在暗淡的煤油灯光的映照下，就好像把地狱翻转过来吊在那里似的，仅凭我的技术，是无法上去的。我想这些老鼠总还不至于从那么高的地方降下来吧，所以我决定解除这方面的警戒。即使这样，我还是担心存在三面受攻击的危险。如果只来一伙，我闭着眼睛也对付得了，如果来两伙，我自信总还可以想办法解决，但是如果来三伙，那么不管我怎样被人称为本能的捕鼠能手，也无从下手。

paragraphs.source_en: Nevertheless, to ask Kuro from the rickshaw man's house to come help me would damage my dignity. What was I to do? I thought and thought, but no good idea came to me; the best course was to decide that such a thing would not happen, and thereby gain peace of mind. People who have no remedy always like to think, "Such a thing will not happen." Just look at the real world: a bride married yesterday might die today, yet the new bridegroom sings praises of growing old together and shows not the slightest sign of worry. People do not refrain from worrying because there is nothing worth worrying about, but because worrying, however much one does it, is of no use. In my own case, I certainly lacked strong grounds for proving that a three-sided attack would not occur; but under the circumstances, assuming it would not occur was highly useful in relieving my anxiety. For all creatures, peace of mind is necessary, and I naturally desired peace of mind as well. Therefore, I decided that no three-sided attack would occur.

units.source_en: Nevertheless, to ask Kuro from the rickshaw man's house to come help me would damage my dignity.
units.source_zh: 虽然如此，可是请车夫家的老黑来帮我的忙，又有损于我的威信。

units.source_en: What was I to do?
units.source_zh: 这该怎么办呢？

units.source_en: I thought and thought, but no good idea came to me; the best course was to decide that such a thing would not happen, and thereby gain peace of mind.
units.source_zh: 我想来想去，想不出个好主意，最好的办法就是认定不会发生这种事儿，求得放心。

units.source_en: People who have no remedy always like to think, "Such a thing will not happen."

units.source_zh: 那些没办法的人总是喜欢这样想：“这种事是不会发生的。”

units.source_en: Just look at the real world: a bride married yesterday might die today, yet the new bridegroom sings praises of growing old together and shows not the slightest sign of worry.

units.source_en: People do not refrain from worrying because there is nothing worth worrying about, but because worrying, however much one does it, is of no use.

units.source_zh: 人们不担心，倒不是不值得担心，而是因为再担心也毫无用处。

units.source_en: In my own case, I certainly lacked strong grounds for proving that a three-sided attack would not occur; but under the circumstances, assuming it would not occur was highly useful in relieving my anxiety.
units.source_zh: 我固然缺乏不会发生受三面攻击的有力论据，但就情况而论，认定它不会发生，这对于解除我的担心是十分有用的。

units.source_en: For all creatures, peace of mind is necessary, and I naturally desired peace of mind as well.
units.source_zh: 对于万物来说，放心都是必要的，我当然也希望能够放心。

units.source_en: Therefore, I decided that no three-sided attack would occur.
units.source_zh: 因此，我认定不会三面受攻击。

paragraphs.source_zh: 虽然如此，可是请车夫家的老黑来帮我的忙，又有损于我的威信。这该怎么办呢？我想来想去，想不出个好主意，最好的办法就是认定不会发生这种事儿，求得放心。那些没办法的人总是喜欢这样想：“这种事是不会发生的。”各位不妨看看现实社会，昨天娶的新娘说不定今天就会死去，而新姑爷却大唱什么白头偕老的赞歌，丝毫也看不出担心的样子。人们不担心，倒不是不值得担心，而是因为再担心也毫无用处。我固然缺乏不会发生受三面攻击的有力论据，但就情况而论，认定它不会发生，这对于解除我的担心是十分有用的。对于万物来说，放心都是必要的，我当然也希望能够放心。因此，我认定不会三面受攻击。
